rationale.conceptual: The paper's method is a custom configuration of a stationary dust-driven wind model involving several interacting components (SiO nucleation rate recalibration, vapour pressure, dust growth, flux-averaged extinction). It demands genuine understanding of astrophysical dust condensation theory and non-trivial numerical implementation. It is not an off-the-shelf recipe, and subtle mistakes in translating the physics would break the results.
rationale.execution: The reproduction pipeline includes extracting and refitting laboratory nucleation data (Step 1) and then implementing a full wind model solver with opacity lookups and iterative shooting. This amounts to a multi-step computational workflow with data acquisition (Ossenkopf et al. opacities) and multiple input sources. However, the process can be consolidated into a single well-structured script, and the tooling requirements (Python/numerics) are standard, placing it at the mid-range of execution difficulty.
